note: Case files for the diagnosis lab. Every case runs on the same illustrative system: 12 V, 200 Ah LiFePO4, an 800 W panel array, 4.5 peak sun hours. The gate checks that each case's evidence is really what the meter reads, so every case is solvable. The diagnosis list is shown in alphabetical order, and two entries (the inverter, a too-thin cable) are decoys no case uses.

diagnoses.label: The main fuse has blown
diagnoses.why: Volts reach the battery side of the fuse but not the other side. A fuse is a wire that must pass current; with the power off, a good one shows a few milliohms and a blown one shows OL.

diagnoses.label: A battery post connection is corroded or loose
diagnoses.why: A bad joint drops volts only while current flows through it. Measure across the joint under load: a good one reads millivolts, a bad one reads volts.

diagnoses.label: The panel is not connected to the battery
diagnoses.why: In full sun the battery sits at its own voltage (it is not being charged), while the panel reads its open-circuit voltage instead of its working voltage.

diagnoses.label: The negative lead is broken
diagnoses.why: Measuring volts across a break in a lead that should carry current reads the whole battery voltage across the gap. Both sides of the fuse read normal, so the positive side is fine.

diagnoses.label: A battery cell has failed
diagnoses.why: A battery that reads far below its resting voltage for its charge, and sags under load, has a failed cell. The fuse, cable and inverter are blameless; the inverter switches off on low volts.

diagnoses.label: The inverter has failed
diagnoses.why: Not supported: an inverter fault would leave the DC readings normal and still pass power to the fuse and cable.

diagnoses.label: The cable is too thin for the load
diagnoses.why: Not supported: a too-thin cable drops volts in proportion to the current. Measure across the cable under load and compare.

cases.title: Everything went dark
cases.symptom: At 20:00 the lights, the router and the TV all went off together. The battery monitor still shows plenty of charge.

evidence.what: DC volts, battery side of the fuse to the negative post
DC volts, inverter side of the fuse to the negative post

cases.title: Dim lights when the pump runs
cases.symptom: At 07:30 the pump starts and the lights dim; the battery monitor shows 90%.

evidence.what: DC volts across the positive post connection while the loads run

cases.title: The batteries never recharge
cases.symptom: Three sunny days and the monitor falls a little more every night. It is 12:00 now and the sun is out.

evidence.what: DC volts across the battery (not being charged: under 13.8 V)

cases.title: Dead outlet, good fuse
cases.symptom: At 20:00 the outlet is dead and the DC lights are out. The fuse looks fine and the battery monitor shows a healthy charge.

evidence.what: DC volts across the main fuse's far side to the negative post (still the battery voltage)
DC volts across the gap in the negative lead

cases.title: The inverter trips on the kettle
cases.symptom: At 07:06 the kettle goes on and the inverter shuts down. The monitor says 80%, and the fuse and cable look fine.

evidence.what: DC volts across the battery posts (a healthy 80% battery rests near 13.2 V)
